papers.title_in_file: Advancing quantum technology workforce: industry insights into qualification and training needs
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, study design, limitations, results on talent shortage.
papers.what_it_is: An interview and questionnaire study of quantum industry workforce and training needs.

assertions.value: The authors report that industry representatives from 12 out of 34 companies mention the talent shortage or the difficulty of attracting talent, across all types of companies.
quotes: Industry representatives from 12 out of 34 companies mention the talent shortage or the difficulty of attracting talent, representing all types of companies.
assertions.certainty_reason: Interview count from one qualitative study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the findings are based on 34 semi-structured interviews with industry representatives and a follow-up questionnaire.
quotes: The findings are based on 34 semi-structured interviews with industry representatives and a follow-up questionnaire to validate some of the issues raised in the interviews.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that they cannot expect a complete or representative picture of the QT industry, and that the responses are expected to be biased because all companies were already active in QT.
quotes: However, we cannot expect to get a complete or representative picture of the QT industry.
Therefore, it is expected that the responses are biased
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.

papers.title_in_file: PANSATZ: Pulse-based Ansatz for Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, approach, results, hardware experiment, conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A pulse-level parameterized ansatz for VQE, tested in simulation and on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report achieving chemical accuracy in simulation for several molecules and on one of IBM's NISQ devices for the H2 molecule in the STO3G basis.
quotes: We manage to achieve chemical accuracy both in simulation for several molecules and on one of IBM's NISQ devices for the H2 molecule in the STO3G basis.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one molecule on hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report significant latency reduction compared with a gate-based ansatz.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, page 1; the abstract also gives a factor up to seven, not quoted here
quotes: Our results are compared to a gate-based ansatz and show significant latency reduction
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that use of PANSATZ in algorithms with problem-inspired ansatze such as QAOA remains to be considered, and that for LiH one layer is not expressive enough for large atomic distances.
quotes: The use of PANSATZ in quantum algorithms where problem-inspired ansatze are used, such as QAOA, remains to be considered.
For the LiH molecule, 1 layer is not expressive enough for large atomic distances
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope and limits.

papers.what_it_is: Applies pulse-efficient transpilation to QNN classification, quantum kernel digit recognition and the Hamiltonian Variational Ansatz on IBM devices.

assertions.value: The authors report that pulse-efficient transpilation reduces average circuit durations and significantly improves classification accuracy, in binary classification on a synthetic dataset with quantum neural networks and in handwritten digit recognition with quantum kernel estimation.
quotes: In both cases, we find that pulse-efficient transpilation vastly reduces average circuit durations and, as a result, significantly improves classification accuracy.
We report results for two standard experiments: binary classification on a synthetic dataset with quantum neural networks and handwritten digit recognition with quantum kernel estimation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that combining pulse-efficient transpilation with dynamical decoupling allowed kernels up to 9 qubits and 90% classification accuracy, while regular circuits remain below 80%.
quotes: Combining PE transpilation with dynamical decoupling allowed us to accurately estimate kernels up to 9 qubits and achieve 90% classification accuracy, whilst regular circuits remain below 80%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that their experiments ran on three different IBM Quantum backends using qiskit, and that extension to other protocols with parameterized RZX gates is an expectation.
quotes: we conduct our experiments across three different IBM Quantum [42] backends using qiskit [43].
We expect that these improvements extend to most protocols featuring parameterized RZX
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.

papers.title_in_file: Dequantizing quantum machine learning models using tensor networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, sections III to VII, parts of appendices.
papers.what_it_is: A tensor-network analysis of when variational QML model function classes can be dequantized by classical MPS models.

assertions.value: The paper proves that any VQML model employing a general encoding strategy and a circuit ansatz can be represented as an MPS model (Theorem 1).
quotes: Theorem 1 (Any VQML model is a MPS model). Any VQML model employing a general encoding strategy E, and a circuit ansatz U such as Eq. (1) can be represented as an MPS model:
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a theorem with proof in the appendix.

assertions.value: The authors state that a non-dequantizable VQML function requires a function space of an exponentially large dimension and a highly entangled coefficient on this function space, and that the first statement of their summary is rigorous while the second and third rest on numerical evidence.
quotes: Note that while the first statement is rigorous, the second and third are based on numerical evidence corresponding to Figs. 3,4 and 5.
So informally, a non-dequantizable VQML function requires a function space of an exponentially large dimension and a highly entangled coefficient on this function space.
assertions.certainty_reason: Informal conclusion partly resting on numerical evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that the dequantization concept in this work relates to the expressivity of machine-learning function classes and does not directly correlate with other aspects such as generalizability or sample complexity during training (trainability).
quotes: We again emphasize that the dequantization concept discussed in this work relates to the expressivity of machine-learning function classes and does not directly correlate with other aspects of dequantization, such as generalizability or sample complexity during training (trainability).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, sections 3 to 6 including results discussion and conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A framework that searches circuit structures for interconnected QPUs, using TeleGate and TeleData and training-free evaluation, on three VQE tasks.

assertions.value: The authors report that optimal solutions were achieved for the ground state energy of the BeH2 molecule, the Heisenberg model and the transverse-field Ising model, although only a small set of circuits are trained during the QAS workflow.
quotes: The optimal solutions have been achieved for these problems, although only a small set of circuits are trained during the entire QAS workflow.
computing the ground state energy of the BeH2 molecule, the Heisenberg model and the transverse-field Ising model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study on three tasks.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for BeH2 with the TeleGate method, with Ng = 40 the gap to the optimal solution is 0.0030, slightly larger than the chemical accuracy threshold, and that 13 optimal solutions are found at 50 gates and 79 at 60.
quotes: With Ng = 40, the gap between the found solution and the optimal one is 0.0030, slightly larger than the chemical accuracy threshold. As Ng increases to 50, 13 optimal solutions are found, and this number rises to 79 when Ng increases to 60.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study (simulation).

assertions.value: The authors state that efficacy is demonstrated through numerical experiments on three VQE tasks, and propose incorporating elements of the VAns method to better address larger-scale circuit search problems.
quotes: Through numerical experiments on three VQE tasks, the efficacy and efficiency of our scheme is demonstrated.
To better address largerscale quantum circuit search problems, we can incorporate elements of the VAns method [25] into our framework.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.

papers.title_in_file: Robustness of quantum algorithms against coherent control errors
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section II, discussion of guideline, conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A Lipschitz-bound framework for worst-case fidelity of circuits under coherent control errors.

assertions.value: The authors derive worst-case fidelity bounds which show that resilience against coherent control errors is mainly influenced by the norms of the Hamiltonians generating the individual gates.
quotes: We derive worst-case fidelity bounds which show that the resilience against coherent control errors is mainly influenced by the norms of the Hamiltonians generating the individual gates.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived analytically.

assertions.value: The authors report that, using the 3-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform as an example, the guideline of reducing Hamiltonian norms targets robustness more effectively than existing guidelines based on circuit depth or gate count.
quotes: Using the 3-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform as an example application, we demonstrate that this guideline targets robustness more effectively than existing ones based on circuit depth or gate count.
assertions.certainty_reason: Demonstrated on one small example.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Lipschitz bound (17) is in general not tight, since the coupling between sequentially applied gates is not taken into account.
quotes: It is important to note that the Lipschitz bound (17) itself is, in general, not tight, e.g., since the coupling between sequentially applied gates is not taken into account.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limit.

papers.title_in_file: Predominant Aspects on Security for Quantum Machine Learning: Literature Review
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methodology, sections IV to VII.
papers.what_it_is: A systematic literature review of vulnerabilities and defenses of quantum machine learning models.

assertions.value: The authors state that the survey reveals that while QML possesses unique strengths, it also introduces novel attack vectors not seen in classical systems.
quotes: The survey reveals that while QML possesses unique strengths, it also introduces novel attack vectors not seen in classical systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review synthesis of other authors' work.

assertions.value: The authors report that the systematic search identified 4 658 records and that in total 27 records are included in the literature research results.
quotes: Upon execution of the systematic search as depicted above 4 658 records were identified.
In total 27 records are included in the literature research results.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own review procedure and counts.

assertions.value: The authors state that some defense mechanisms have been proposed in the literature but require further empirical studies to determine their reliability and effectiveness.
quotes: Some defense mechanisms have been proposed in literature, but require further empirical studies to determine their reliability and effectiveness.
assertions.certainty_reason: Reviewer's statement without a dedicated test in the paper.

papers.title_in_file: Training variational quantum algorithms with random gate activation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, main text through discussion; supplemental material only skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A training scheme that activates two-qubit gates at random and progressively, tested on the XXZ ground state problem.

assertions.value: The authors report that for random activation training, much fewer trials are trapped in bad local minima and the averaged VQE energy is much lower than for plain training, across 500 independent optimization trials on a 12-qubit system.
assertions.anchor: Main text, VQE results comparison, Fig. 2
quotes: For the RA training, there are much fewer trials trapped in the bad local minima and the averaged VQE energy is much lower than that obtained from the plain training as shown in Fig. 2.
The results consist of 500 independent optimization trials on a 12qubit system.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that roughly 500 times fewer quantum gates are used for random activation training in their experiments, and that obtained energies are substantially improved in noisy VQE settings.
quotes: roughly 500 times less quantum gates are used for RA training
We show experimental results on noisy VQE settings, and the obtained energies are substantially improved when using RA training
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study; noisy results are in the supplement.

assertions.value: The authors state that they apply the algorithm to the ground state energy problem of the one-dimensional antiferromagnetic XXZ model, and claim it can be naturally applied to other tasks and other flavors of VQAs.
quotes: we utilize the new proposed training algorithm to solve the ground state energy problem of the one-dimensional (1D) antiferromagnetic XXZ model
This new algorithm can be naturally applied to other practical tasks and other flavors of VQAs due to its universal form.
assertions.certainty_reason: Tested on one model only; wider applicability is an author claim.
